data.name: Lorencia
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'Laurus', meaning laurel, a tree often used as a symbol of triumph and victory in ancient Rome. In Christianity, the name Lorencia is associated with Saint Lorencia, a Christian martyr who is said to have been crowned with laurel wreaths before her execution.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes triumph, victory, and the rewards of spiritual dedication.
data.numerology_meaning: Influential, intuitive, creative, and high-achieving individuals.

in_hebrew.name: לורנציה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לורנציה היא שם שמקורו בלטינית, ומשמעותו 'חסידות'. השם נקשר לעקדה, שהייתה אשה ישראלית, והייתה ידועה בחסדה ובנאמנות. השם הפך לפופולרי בעקבותיו פעל, שהיה בן דודו של ישו. במסורת הנוצרית, השם 'לורנציה' מסמל חסידות, תקווה וקדושה.

in_greek.name: Λορεντία
in_greek.long_meaning: Λορεντία είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την Λατινική, με σημασία την 'Ελπίδα'. Η λέξη συνδέεται με την Ακηδία, μια γυναίκα της Εβραϊκής Βίβλου, η οποία ήταν γνωστή για την ελπίδα της, την χάρη της και την αθανασία της. Το όνομα έγινε δημοφιλές λόγω του προηγουμένου του, ο οποίος ήταν εγγονός του βαπτιστή. Στη Νεοελληνική Βίβλο, το όνομα 'Λορεντία' σημαίνει ελπίδα, χάρη, αγάπη και αθάνατο.

in_latin.name: Lorencia
in_latin.long_meaning: Lorencia est nomen quod a Latina provenit, significans 'Fides'. Nomen hunc connectamus cum Acedia, quae in Biblia Veteri mentionatur, quae fuit nota sua fide, gratia, et immortalitate. Nomen hanc populare fecit predecessor eius, qui erat nepos Ioannis Baptistae. In Ecclesia Catholica, nomen 'Lorencia' significat fidem, gratiam, fidem, sanctitatem, et immortalitatem.

in_english.name: Lorencia
in_english.long_meaning: Lorencia is a name derived from Latin, meaning 'Hope'. The name is connected to Acedia, a woman mentioned in the Old Testament, who was known for her hope, charity, and immortality. The name became popular due to her predecessor, who was the nephew of John the Baptist. In the Christian tradition, the name 'Lorencia' symbolizes hope, charity, faithfulness, holiness, and immortality.

historical_references.reference: Lorencia of the Thebaid, also known as Saint Lorentia or Saint Laurence of Thebes, is believed to be a martyr who lived during the 3rd or 4th century. She is said to have been born in Egypt and was the daughter of a pagan nobleman. According to legend, she was converted to Christianity by Saint Anthony the Great, who was her uncle. After her father's death, she renounced her inheritance and gave it to the poor. She was arrested for her faith and, during her imprisonment, was subjected to various tortures including having her breasts cut off. Miraculously, they grew back whole. She was eventually beheaded and her body was taken to Constantinople and buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles.

The name Lorencia is sometimes associated with this legend, as it is said that she was one of the virgins in Ursula's retinue.
